intro: Chiropractors combine hands-on treatment with clinical judgment and patient education, skills used in teaching and allied health. The closest of the 25 careers below is Midwives, with a 76% match, while Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary are 73% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $107,310, or 35% more than the $79,200 chiropractors earn.
why_it_works: A treatment day means assessing pain, adjusting the spine and joints and teaching patients exercises and habits. O*NET rates complex problem solving, judgment and social perceptiveness at 3.88 out of 5 for this job. Teaching, athletic training and orthotics use the same knowledge of the body. Every match needs no more education than you have. The gaps are instructing and coordination.
tips: Teaching anatomy or clinical skills at a college pays more and uses your training directly.
Orthotists and Prosthetists earn $81,110, which is 2% more, and are a 70% match.
Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470, or 86% more, after a certificate program.

faq.q: What jobs can former chiropractors do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Midwives (76%), Athletic Trainers (73%) and postsecondary health specialties teachers (73%), based on O*NET 31.0. Nursing instructors are 72% matched and earn $80,250, which is 1% more than the $79,200 chiropractor median, and teach in a clinical setting much like yours.

faq.q: Which careers for chiropractors pay more?
faq.a: 14 of the 25 matches pay more. Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470 (86% more), health specialties teachers $107,310 (35% more) and medical scientists $103,410 (31% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Medical science usually involves research training, and dosimetry needs a certificate program.

faq.q: Do chiropractors need another degree to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than chiropractors already have, including all of the top 10. A master's degree is common in close matches, held by 54% of workers in one, so your doctor of chiropractic degree covers most requirements.

The skills that most often need work are instructing, troubleshooting, coordination and operations analysis. Service orientation already rates 3.75 out of 5 for chiropractors in O*NET, so teaching groups and running programs are the main steps outside private practice.
